## Structure and components

- [statement] The Bayesian Market Filters page contains conflicting descriptions: its repository description advertises walk-forward validation, while the audited README says the models were fitted once and frozen. The audit also says that unsupported passive fills and execution delay undermine the reported positive results; treat this as implementation evidence, not a validated trading edge. (low confidence) — https://github.com/AnshDani2004/bayesian-market-filters · keywords: Five-minute volatility-regime-conditioned signal selection

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Pindza reports severe regime dependence for the LightGBM model in a study targeting five-minute forward returns: apparent predictive content concentrates in calm, trending markets and disappears during stress. This is a study-specific warning, not proof that a volatility filter creates profitable SOL trades. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute volatility-regime-conditioned signal selection
- [statement] Methodological inference: compare any volatility-conditioned selector with a static baseline using chronological, purged walk-forward evaluation, and report stress-regime performance separately. RegimeNAS supplies the adaptive design precedent, while the Frontiers study shows why pooled performance and unpurged evaluation can conceal regime-dependent failure. This is a proposed evaluation design, not demonstrated SOL profitability. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2508.11338v1 · keywords: Five-minute volatility-regime-conditioned signal selection · also: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Pindza defines the descriptive volatility regimes by realized volatility relative to its sample median and reports higher spread proxies, trade intensity, and depth imbalance in the high-volatility regime. The paper describes a range-based spread proxy rather than measured executable bid-ask quotes. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute volatility-regime-conditioned signal selection
- [statement] The Bayesian Market Filters repository provides a concrete causal regime-estimation pattern: fit a two-state HMM on the initial training data and use forward filtering probabilities rather than smoothed probabilities during the backtest. Its data and backtest are hourly BTC, not five-minute SOL. (low confidence) — https://github.com/AnshDani2004/bayesian-market-filters · keywords: Five-minute volatility-regime-conditioned signal selection
- [statement] RegimeNAS provides a candidate selector architecture: regime probabilities condition the weighting or selection of specialized modules. This is a model design precedent, rather than an executable five-minute SOL result. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2508.11338v1 · keywords: Five-minute volatility-regime-conditioned signal selection
- [statement] Zhivkov and Kandilarov report complete TEMA-BTC testing failure across all optimizers. Their experiment uses an hourly timeframe, includes SOL among the tested assets, assumes zero transaction costs, and has a single-run exploratory design; it provides adjacent evidence of strategy breakdown rather than five-minute SOL validation. (low confidence) — https://www.mdpi.com/2227-7390/14/5/761 · keywords: Five-minute volatility-regime-conditioned signal selection

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Implementation recommendation: estimate a regime threshold from training or past observations, then apply it forward; do not turn a full-sample descriptive median into a live historical trading filter. Pindza supplies a sample-median regime description, while the Bayesian Market Filters implementation explicitly uses forward probabilities and trains its regime model only on the initial sample. (medium confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/blockchain/articles/10.3389/fbloc.2026.1811716/full · keywords: Five-minute volatility-regime-conditioned signal selection · also: https://github.com/AnshDani2004/bayesian-market-filters
- [statement] Wen and coauthors report that intraday momentum and reversal patterns change with price jumps, announcement events, and liquidity. Their study uses hourly cryptocurrency data, so it motivates conditional signal selection without validating a five-minute SOL decision rule. (low confidence) — https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1062940822000833 · keywords: Five-minute volatility-regime-conditioned signal selection
- [statement] The Crypto quant research README lists a momentum strategy with a volatility-regime filter as a candidate requiring a fresh precommitted hypothesis. That statement is a research proposal, not a successful test of regime-conditioned signal selection. (low confidence) — https://github.com/anthonychungwork-byte/crypto_quant_research · keywords: Five-minute volatility-regime-conditioned signal selection
- [statement] The intraday forecasting-horizon study explicitly distinguishes variability across repeated model runs from uncertainty due to temporal dependence and changing regimes, and calls for rolling-window or block-bootstrap intervals. Repeated-seed standard deviations therefore should not be read as evidence that a selected regime strategy generalizes across market conditions. (low confidence) — https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/applied-mathematics-and-statistics/articles/10.3389/fams.2026.1888767/full · keywords: Five-minute volatility-regime-conditioned signal selection
- [statement] RegimeNAS evaluated daily cryptocurrency OHLCV data. Its reported forecast improvements therefore do not directly validate a five-minute SOL signal selector; testing that transfer remains necessary. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2508.11338v1 · keywords: Five-minute volatility-regime-conditioned signal selection
